notes_list.title: Wacker Oxidation
notes_list.basic_overview: Terminal alkenes can be oxidized to methyl ketones under palladium(II)-catalysed oxidative conditions, commonly involving PdCl2 and a copper/oxygen regeneration system.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
For a simple terminal alkene RCH=CH2, the usual Wacker product is RCOCH3. The reaction proceeds through alkene coordination, nucleophilic water addition and oxidation-related steps.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Terminal alkenes can be oxidized to methyl ketones under palladium(II)-catalysed oxidative conditions, commonly involving PdCl2 and a copper/oxygen regeneration system. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
